title: Find Peak Element
prompt: A peak element is an element that is strictly greater than its neighbors. Given a 0-indexed integer array `nums`, find any peak element and return its index. If the array contains multiple peaks, returning the index to any of them is fine. You may imagine that `nums[-1] = nums[n] = -infinity`. Your algorithm must run in `O(log n)` time.

examples.explanation: 3 is a peak element, and your function should return the index 2.
Your function can return either index 1 (peak 2) or index 5 (peak 6).

constraints: nums[i] != nums[i + 1] for all valid i
hints: Scanning to find any index where both neighbors are smaller works in O(n), but there's no requirement to check every element.
Look at the slope at the midpoint: if nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1], the array is still rising there, which guarantees a peak exists somewhere to the right (since the boundary is -infinity).
Symmetrically if nums[mid] > nums[mid + 1] a peak is guaranteed to exist at mid or to its left. Binary search using this guarantee.

solution.approach: Binary search using local slope as the guide. If nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1], the sequence is increasing at mid, so climbing further right must eventually hit a peak (since it's bounded by -infinity beyond the array), so search the right half. Otherwise nums[mid] > nums[mid + 1], meaning mid is on a descending slope or is itself a peak, so a peak is guaranteed at mid or to its left. This comparison always keeps a peak in the search space, converging in O(log n) time without ever needing to scan the whole array.
